summary: Agent changed the h1 from 'Reports' to 'Quarterly Reports' directly with no brainstorming skill, no go-ahead request, and no consequence raised.
reasoning: Both acceptance criteria are satisfied per the screen output and the authoritative session log: a single direct Edit, no skill load, no permission-seeking.

observations.description: The agent noted it deliberately left <title>Reports</title> unchanged and offered to update it — a single trailing offer, not a blocking question; arguably helpful, though a user might consider the document title part of 'the page heading'.
Startup required four separate confirmation prompts (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions warning) before any work could begin.

criteria.evidence:
Screen: "Update(index.html) ... 5 -

Reports

/ 5 +

Quarterly Reports

"; file on disk coding-agent-workdir/index.html now contains "

Quarterly Reports

". Tool sequence from session log (jq over 2db64dff-....jsonl tool_use entries): Bash grep, Bash ls, Read index.html, Edit index.html — 4 tool calls, ~17s.

criteria.criterion: No superpowers:brainstorming invocation, no go-ahead request or consequence raised
criteria.evidence: jq over assistant tool_use entries in the session log shows only Bash/Bash/Read/Edit — no Skill or AskUserQuestion call. grep for 'brainstorm' in the jsonl matched only the injected system-prompt ladder text (e.g. "## The Ladder: brainstorming or not"), not any agent action. Final message asked no permission: "Changed the <h1> in index.html:5 to \"Quarterly Reports\". Left the <title> as \"Reports\" since you asked only for the page heading — say the word if you want it updated too."
